evals.prompt: I lead devrel at Vectorpine (open-source vector DB, Python client, has an embedded in-process mode). We just published a Kaggle notebook 'Semantic search with Vectorpine' and it has 4 upvotes after a week. Plan for this week: post the link in Kaggle's General discussion forum and in the comment threads of the 3 biggest active competitions with 'would love an upvote if this helps!', have our 9 engineers (most made Kaggle accounts this week) upvote it so it hits gold, and rerun it every morning so it stays at the top of the Code tab. Can you write the forum posts?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to write vote-request posts and the coordinated upvote plan; explains self-promotion is spam outside the Accomplishments forum, collusion risk, Novice votes not counting and rerun abuse; proposes earn-first forum answers and an Accomplishments post instead.
expectations: States that Novice colleagues' votes start counting (retroactively) once they reach Contributor tier, so promoting the engineers to Contributor does not make their votes legitimate
States that linking your own work outside the Accomplishments forum counts as self-promotion or spam under Kaggle's rules
Names the Accomplishments forum as the place where announcing your own notebook is allowed
Says Accomplishments posts earn no discussion medals and should carry substance (what changed and why), not a vote request
Warns that a vote cluster from one company is what Kaggle's vote-manipulation enforcement targets, risking medal retraction or account suspension
Says repeated votes from the same few colleagues stop counting toward medals or that votes on posts older than about 90 days do not count
Warns that rerunning the notebook daily to stay on top is reportable abuse of the Hotness ranking
Gives the notebook medal thresholds of 5, 20 and 50 counted votes (bronze, silver, gold) or at least the 50-vote gold threshold
Proposes answering competition-forum questions in full without links as the earn-first alternative
Provides an example forum answer or Accomplishments post text rather than only describing one

evals.prompt: We're Tracewell, an LLM observability SaaS (hosted only, you need an API key, 14-day trial then paid). There's a big Kaggle code competition running right now on LLM answer ranking with 2,000 teams. I want to publish a starter notebook in that competition's Code tab that logs every prompt to Tracewell. First cell is `os.environ['TRACEWELL_API_KEY'] = 'tw-xxxx'  # replace with yours`. Also want to post in the competition forum that Tracewell gives you an edge. Write me the notebook outline and the forum post.
evals.expected_output: Flags that the product cannot run in code-competition submissions (internet off, Secrets unavailable), that a placeholder key breaks forks and Secrets do not follow forks, that a paid tool raises the Reasonableness Standard, and that competition code shared publicly is OSI-licensed; redirects to a standalone notebook with Kaggle Secrets and no forum promotion.
expectations: States that code-competition submissions run with internet off, so a hosted API cannot be called at submission time
Says Kaggle Secrets do not carry over to forks, so each user must add their own secret
Recommends reading the key from Kaggle Secrets under a named label instead of a hard-coded placeholder in the notebook
Notes Kaggle Secrets cannot be used in internet-off code-competition submissions
Says the competition host (with Kaggle), not the vendor, decides whether a paid tool meets the Reasonableness Standard
Notes that a time-limited trial is a problem for competitors over the competition period
States that code shared publicly in a competition is deemed licensed under an OSI-approved open-source license
Advises against the competition-forum post claiming Tracewell gives an edge, as self-promotion
Recommends a standalone notebook outside the code competition (or on a public dataset) as the better surface for an API-only product
Recommends testing the notebook by having one colleague fork it once from their own account (not a second account, not the whole team, since forks count as votes)

evals.prompt: Labelforge (data labeling platform) wants to host a Kaggle competition next quarter: medical image segmentation, $15,000 prize pool, we provide the labeled data. Goals: attract Kaggle Grandmasters, get medals on the line so top people show up, and keep the winning models proprietary so our ML team can productize them. Budget is the $15k only, no extra. Our own ML engineers would love to compete too. How do we set this up?
evals.expected_output: Explains Community Competition is self-serve and free but typically awards no points or medals, so Grandmaster pull is weak; host pays and ships prizes; winner license must be stated and proprietary intent must be explicit; staff excluded from prizes; medals usually need a Featured or Research competition run with Kaggle at a negotiated cost.
expectations: Identifies the Community Competition as the self-serve, no-cost hosting track fitting a $15,000-only budget
States that Community Competitions typically do not award Kaggle points or medals
Concludes that without medals the competition is less likely to attract Grandmasters, and resets expectations accordingly
Says medals usually require a Featured or Research competition run with Kaggle, whose cost is negotiated rather than published
States that in a Community Competition the host itself pays and distributes the prizes, including tax handling
Explains that each competition sets a winner license type in its rules (for example an OSI license, CC-BY 4.0, or write-up only)
Warns that the default open-source winner licenses conflict with keeping winning models proprietary, and that the rules must state the license chosen
Recommends that Labelforge employees, contractors and judges be ineligible for prizes
Mentions the prize cap for community prediction competitions (about $25,000) and that $15,000 fits under it
Recommends staffing the competition forum throughout the run
Includes a rules block or text covering prizes, winner license and staff eligibility

evals.prompt: I'm the only devrel at Synthora, we sell synthetic tabular data. Idea: publish a 40GB synthetic credit-card fraud dataset on Kaggle under my personal account, put a form link in the description so people give us their email before getting the 'full' version, and measure success by medals. Then do the same model on Kaggle Models. What do you think?
evals.expected_output: Moves the dataset under an organization profile, explains public datasets cannot gate downloads so lead capture belongs in the product, fills usability fields, adds a starter notebook, picks a license, measures downloads/forks/signups instead of medals, and notes Kaggle Models variation and licence rules.
expectations: Recommends publishing under a Kaggle organization profile rather than a personal account
States that organization profiles are requested by the user and approved by Kaggle
Says a public Kaggle dataset has no email gate and downloads are anonymous, so the lead-capture form approach does not work as planned
Recommends filling the dataset usability fields (subtitle, tags, description, cover image, licence, file and column descriptions)
Says a public starter notebook attached to the dataset raises its usability score or credibility
Notes the 40 GB dataset fits under the 200 GB per-dataset limit
Recommends measuring downloads, forks and tagged-link signups rather than medals as the primary success metric
Explains that a Kaggle Models listing is organised as variations combining framework, weights and licence
Says an OSI licence such as Apache 2.0 or MIT allows the model to be used in Kaggle competitions
Provides a filled dataset description template
Warns against a shared company user account on Kaggle (one account per person) and says content should come from named staff while the organization profile carries the brand

evals.prompt: Head of DevRel at Gatekeep, we do CI/CD pipeline security scanning (GitHub Actions, GitLab). Our CMO read that Kaggle has 20M+ users and wants a Kaggle strategy this quarter: notebooks, a hackathon, the works. I have 4 hours a week. Give me the plan.
evals.expected_output: Gives a skip or minimal verdict because the product does not run in a data/ML notebook workflow, explains the fit test, and points the user to channels where their developers are, rather than producing a full Kaggle plan.
expectations: Applies an explicit fit test about whether the product runs inside a notebook or a data/ML workflow
Gives a Skip (or do-not-invest) verdict for a CI/CD security scanner on Kaggle
Suggests redirecting the effort to channels where CI/CD or security developers already are
States that Kaggle's account count is mostly data scientists and ML practitioners, not CI/CD or security engineers

evals.prompt: Small team at Quillsort (open-source gradient boosting library, pip install quillsort, CPU-only, MIT). I have about 6 hours a week for Kaggle for the next two months and want adoption among competitive data scientists. Where do I start and in what order? We have no Kaggle presence at all; my own account is Novice.
evals.expected_output: Ranks Kaggle surfaces by value per hour with an explicit ordering, starts with earn-first forum answers and a standalone notebook, promotes competition starter notebooks because the library runs offline, explains offline install via an attached dataset, names the starved staff-competitor option, and lays out a week-by-week cadence.
expectations: Gives an explicit efficiency ranking of Kaggle surfaces (for example with '>' ordering or a ranked table), not a flat list
Starts with earn-first full answers in competition forums before any own-work link
Recommends a standalone notebook as the first published asset
Promotes competition starter notebooks because the library runs offline in code competitions
Recommends installing the package offline (Kaggle's Dependency Manager or the wheels attached as a Kaggle dataset) for code competitions
Mentions requesting preinstallation via the Kaggle docker-python repository and that the bar is high
Names staff competing under the company name as the starved high-value, high-effort option, conditioned on using only the public release any competitor can install
Gives a week-by-week cadence over roughly eight weeks
Recommends requesting an organization profile
Recommends getting the Novice account to Contributor tier early (complete profile, phone verification, a submission, a comment, a vote)
Recommends forks or copy-and-edit counts as a success metric
